customers.name: Home-Care Patient / Resident
customers.description: An older or chronically ill person living at home with several daily medications, often with reduced memory, dexterity, or eyesight. Success means taking exactly the right medicines at the right times, staying safely independent at home, and knowing that if something goes wrong someone will notice and help.
careAbout: Taking the right medicine at the right time, every time
Staying independent at home instead of moving into care
Simple, unmistakable prompts they can follow unaided
Knowing a nurse will be alerted if a dose is missed
Not feeling watched, judged, or a burden
Dignity, privacy, and control over their own routine
winsThem: Clear spoken, written, and light prompts with one large confirmation button
The device only ever releases the correct pouch for that moment
Missed doses are safely locked away, not left lying around
A trusted carer is notified automatically when help is needed
Fewer disruptive home visits at fixed times of day
theirFear: Taking the wrong medicine, a double dose, or missing a critical one
Losing independence and being moved into institutional care
Being alone with no one noticing if something goes wrong

jobsToBeDone.name: Manage my medication safely and stay independent at home
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Turn a complex, error-prone daily medication routine into a guided, reliable ritual the patient can complete on their own at home.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Every scheduled dose is taken correctly and on time, so the patient stays healthy and independent without constant supervision.

steps.step: Get reminded and understand what to take now
steps.description: At each scheduled time the device makes it unmistakable that a dose is due and which one, using sound, light, on-screen text, and spoken instructions the patient can follow unaided.

streamsNeeded.name: Scheduled Dose Dispensing and Confirmation
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Triggers the reminder at the prescribed time and presents the dose with multi-sensory prompts.

streamsNeeded.name: Remote Adherence Monitoring and Care Portal
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Holds the patient's medication schedule that drives when and what is prompted.

customerJourneyStories.name: From daily nurse visits to confident self-dosing at home
customerJourneyStories.summary: A patient who has relied on carers to hand out pills learns to take medication independently with the dispensing device, without feeling abandoned by the care service.

stages.narrative: The patient's medication list has grown complex and the home-care service can no longer sustain multiple daily visits just to hand out pills.

media.title: Home-Care Patient / Resident journey stage 1: Trigger
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 1 of "From daily nurse visits to confident self-dosing at home": Trigger.

stages.narrative: The patient and their family first hear about automated dispensing from their home-care nurse or municipality: a locked device that reminds them and dispenses the right dose, with a carer alerted if anything is missed. Discovery is the awareness moment, not the task itself: they connect the idea to staying independent at home rather than moving into care.

media.title: Home-Care Patient / Resident journey stage 2: Discovery
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 2 of "From daily nurse visits to confident self-dosing at home": Discovery.

stages.narrative: The patient and family weigh whether they can trust a machine with life-critical medication: is it simple enough to use, will a real person still respond, and does it reduce rather than remove human contact. They agree to try it once they see the missed-dose safety net and that the nurse stays in the loop.

media.title: Home-Care Patient / Resident journey stage 3: Evaluation
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 3 of "From daily nurse visits to confident self-dosing at home": Evaluation.

stages.narrative: A nurse installs the device, loads the first pouch roll, and walks the patient through a few dispensing cycles. The patient tests whether the prompts are clear and the confirmation button is easy to press.

media.title: Home-Care Patient / Resident journey stage 4: Trial
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 4 of "From daily nurse visits to confident self-dosing at home": Trial.

stages.narrative: Over the first weeks the patient settles into the rhythm: prompts arrive on time, the correct pouch is released on confirmation, and the household adjusts to fewer fixed-time visits while feeling safely covered.

media.title: Home-Care Patient / Resident journey stage 5: Engagement
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 5 of "From daily nurse visits to confident self-dosing at home": Engagement.

stages.narrative: When the routine proves reliable and the patient regains a sense of control and privacy, both patient and family come to depend on the service and resist going back to manual pill handling.

media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 6 of "From daily nurse visits to confident self-dosing at home": Retention.

productStrategy.vision: Let people with complex medication live safely and independently at home for as long as possible, by making every dose reliable and every problem quickly noticed.

year1.focus: Make the daily dispensing ritual unmistakably clear and dependable for frail users
milestones: Clearer multi-sensory prompts for low-vision and low-dexterity users
Faster, more reliable missed-dose safety-net response
Reduced false alarms that erode patient trust

year3.focus: Extend the safety net with video support so more complex patients can stay home
milestones: Two-way video support available for difficult or high-risk doses
Patient-friendly onboarding that shortens time to confident use
Support for higher-acuity patients previously excluded from home dispensing

year5.focus: Turn medication events into early signals of health change managed at home
milestones: Adherence and behaviour patterns flag deterioration early
Remote vitals monitoring integrated with dosing where clinically useful
Home dispensing normalized as a first-line alternative to institutional care

customers.name: Home-Care Nurse / Carer
customers.description: A home-care nurse or carer responsible for the medication safety of many clients across a district. Instead of driving to each home to hand out pills, they monitor a caseload remotely, respond to alarms, and intervene only when a client genuinely needs help. Success means every client stays correctly medicated with far less time lost to routine visits.
careAbout: Every client on their caseload takes medication safely
Spending time on clients who actually need help, not routine pill drops
Clear, trustworthy alarms that are not drowned in noise
Fast ways to resolve a missed dose without always driving out
A complete, defensible record of what happened and when
Not being overwhelmed by an ever-growing caseload
winsThem: A single portal showing every client's adherence and open alarms
Alarms that carry enough context to act without a visit
Remote resolution tools: message the device, connect by video, reschedule
Automatic logging so documentation is not extra manual work
Confidence that missed doses are contained, not lost
theirFear: A serious medication error slipping through unnoticed on their caseload
Alarm fatigue causing a real emergency to be missed
Being held accountable without a clear record of what happened

customerJourneyStories.name: From a 50-device pilot to a service the council relies on
customerJourneyStories.summary: A municipal home-care manager takes automated dispensing from a small pilot to a population-scale service, and builds the evidence base that keeps it funded.

stages.narrative: Rising demand and an unfillable staffing gap force the manager to find a way to deliver safe medication to more people with the same workforce.

media.title: Care-Provider / Municipality Manager journey stage 1: Trigger
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 1 of "From a 50-device pilot to a service the council relies on": Trigger.

stages.narrative: The manager encounters automated dispensing through peer municipalities, procurement frameworks, and vendor case studies showing high adherence and reduced visits. Discovery is the awareness moment, not the task itself: they connect the model to their safety and staffing problem.

media.title: Care-Provider / Municipality Manager journey stage 2: Discovery
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 2 of "From a 50-device pilot to a service the council relies on": Discovery.

stages.narrative: Procurement scrutinises clinical safety, regulatory posture, data protection, integration effort, and total cost-to-serve, and weighs the vendor's ability to support a full rollout rather than just a pilot.

media.title: Care-Provider / Municipality Manager journey stage 3: Evaluation
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 3 of "From a 50-device pilot to a service the council relies on": Evaluation.

stages.narrative: A bounded pilot proves the deployment model: devices provisioned, pharmacy supply flowing, staff trained, and early adherence and visit-avoidance data captured.

media.title: Care-Provider / Municipality Manager journey stage 4: Trial
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 4 of "From a 50-device pilot to a service the council relies on": Trial.

stages.narrative: The service scales across teams and districts, with fleet operations, pharmacy logistics, and monitoring holding up under population load and compliance kept demonstrable.

media.title: Care-Provider / Municipality Manager journey stage 5: Engagement
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 5 of "From a 50-device pilot to a service the council relies on": Engagement.

stages.narrative: Armed with population-level safety and savings evidence, the manager secures renewal and expansion, and the service becomes core infrastructure for the care organisation.

media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 6 of "From a 50-device pilot to a service the council relies on": Retention.

customers.name: Pharmacy Dose-Packaging Partner
customers.description: A pharmacy or dose-dispensing service that produces the patient-specific multi-dose pouch rolls the devices dispense. Success means every roll is accurate, correctly sequenced, and delivered in time to keep devices stocked, with orders tied cleanly to prescriptions and the right device.
careAbout: Every pouch roll matches the patient's current prescription exactly
Rolls sequenced and formatted so the device can dispense them
Orders delivered in time to keep each device stocked
Prescription changes reflected without dangerous lag
A recurring, predictable dose-packaging volume
Clean reconciliation between what was ordered, packed, and dispensed
winsThem: Orders that arrive structured and tied to prescription and device
Pouch formatting compatible with the dispensing hardware
Clear signals when a device needs a fresh roll
Fast, safe handling of prescription changes mid-cycle
Reconciliation data that closes the loop on every roll
theirFear: Packing a roll that does not match the patient's real prescription
A device running out of medication because a roll was late
A prescription change missed between order and packing

customerJourneyStories.name: Turning dispensing devices into a reliable pouch-packing channel
customerJourneyStories.summary: A dose-dispensing pharmacy integrates with the service so its multi-dose pouch production is driven cleanly by device-linked, prescription-accurate orders.

stages.narrative: A growing base of devices in the region creates steady demand for accurate, device-compatible pouch rolls the pharmacy wants to supply.

media.title: Pharmacy Dose-Packaging Partner journey stage 1: Trigger
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 1 of "Turning dispensing devices into a reliable pouch-packing channel": Trigger.

stages.narrative: The pharmacy learns that the dispensing service can drive its dose-packaging orders directly, tied to prescriptions and devices. Discovery is the awareness moment, not the task itself: they see a recurring, structured packing channel rather than ad-hoc requests.

media.title: Pharmacy Dose-Packaging Partner journey stage 2: Discovery
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 2 of "Turning dispensing devices into a reliable pouch-packing channel": Discovery.

stages.narrative: The pharmacy assesses whether order data is accurate and device-compatible, how prescription changes are handled, and whether reconciliation will hold up for safety and audit before committing capacity.

media.title: Pharmacy Dose-Packaging Partner journey stage 3: Evaluation
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 3 of "Turning dispensing devices into a reliable pouch-packing channel": Evaluation.

stages.narrative: With a first cohort of patients, the pharmacy packs device-linked rolls, tests formatting compatibility, and validates that changes and reconciliation work end to end.

media.title: Pharmacy Dose-Packaging Partner journey stage 4: Trial
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 4 of "Turning dispensing devices into a reliable pouch-packing channel": Trial.

stages.narrative: Order intake, packing, delivery, and reconciliation settle into a dependable cycle keyed to device stock levels and current prescriptions.

media.title: Pharmacy Dose-Packaging Partner journey stage 5: Engagement
media.alt: Enterprise journey panel for stage 5 of "Turning dispensing devices into a reliable pouch-packing channel": Engagement.

stages.narrative: As the device base grows into predictable recurring volume with low error rates, the pharmacy treats the service as a core dose-packaging channel.
